analysis: The trial executed successfully but reduced macro validation HR@10 to 0.4775: −0.0262 versus the stated current 0.5037 and −0.0275 versus baseline 0.505. Category HR@10 was Movies_and_TV 0.515, Industrial_and_Scientific 0.520, Electronics 0.375, and CDs_and_Vinyl 0.500. All four declined versus the supplied current category references; Electronics remained below its 0.420 baseline. Thus, mining 64 hard negatives plus 192 random negatives from a 1,024-item pool did not improve this configuration. Biased negative selection without sampling correction may have changed the training objective unfavorably, but the available results do not establish the cause. No epoch traces were supplied to diagnose convergence or checkpoint timing. Reported allocated GPU time was 510.52 seconds.
code_summary: One independently trained SASRec model per category, with 96-dimensional embeddings, two causal Transformer blocks, two attention heads, dropout 0.2, and maximum history length 64. A jointly trained causal history-attention branch shares item embeddings and merges with Transformer features through a learned gate. Scores use normalized sequence/item embeddings, a learned bounded scale, and jointly trained item biases. Training selects at most 24 transitions per history, applies recency weights with an eight-transition half-life, and normalizes losses per history. Each batch draws up to 1,024 distinct uniform items, excludes complete training histories and positive targets, then selects 64 highest-scoring eligible negatives and 192 uniform remaining negatives for ordinary sampled-softmax cross-entropy. AdamW, seed 42, fixed validation candidates, and validation-selected checkpoints are retained. Prediction strictly reconstructs exactly one checkpoint per category with dataset routing and reload parity checks; no ensembles or separately fitted scorers are used.
